newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek farm minister has no new offer for farmers.
newsitem.headline: Greek farm minister has no new offer for farmers.

text.p: Greece's socialist government has no new offers for protesting farmers and they should lift their national road blockade, Agriculture Minister Stephanos Tzoumakas told reporters.
He spoke after an emergency cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Costas Simitis to decide on a government response to the farmers' national road and rail blockade which began seven days ago.
The blockade has stranded hundreds of international and domestic lorries, started to push up food prices and dealt a heavy blow to the economy.

"The positions of the government are known. We have nothing new to propose (to the farmers)," Tzoumakas said. "Those who have erected blockades should assume their responsibilities, remove them and free the roads," he said.
Tzoumakas will go to the heart of the farmers' rebellion in the western mainland town of Larissa on Wednesday to meet local government prefects and farmers' representatives.
His statements were greeted with vows by the farmers to keep up their blockade until Christmas and beyond.
